clips.title: Time Travel Tests! Testing Async Workflows, Signals, and Queries with Temporal
clips.why: How to replace activities with mocks in a workflow test, so the test checks the workflow's logic and nothing outside it.
look: The mocked activity returns a fixed answer, and the workflow cannot tell it is not the real one.
The example is in Go; in TypeScript the mocks are simply the functions you pass to Worker.create.
clips.after: Our fakes for notify and parkTicket record what they would post, so a test can count the reminders.

clips.title: Temporal with Go Tutorial for Beginners: Workflows, Activities, Workers and Testing
clips.why: One minute on testing workflows with Temporal's test environment, where timers do not make the test wait.
look: A workflow with a timer is tested without waiting for it.
The test environment replaces the server; the workflow code is the real one.
clips.after: TestWorkflowEnvironment.createTimeSkipping() is the TypeScript version of the same environment.

clips.title: Move Fast WITHOUT Breaking Anything - Workflow Versioning with Temporal
clips.why: Why you test a change by replaying real histories, and how that catches a change that would break running workflows before it is deployed.
look: Histories from real runs are the test data.
A replay with the new code fails if the code no longer fits the history.
clips.after: Our replay test runs on every pull request with the histories in test/histories.

clips.title: Debugging Temporal Workflows with History Replay
clips.why: A saved history is also a debugging tool: replay it on your laptop and step through the workflow as it ran.
look: The history is downloaded from a real run and replayed locally.
Breakpoints in workflow code stop during the replay, with the real values from the run.
clips.after: When a run of ticketToPr behaves strangely, its history can be replayed the same way, with no VM and no Jira.

practice.q: Start the test server that jumps over timers, once for the whole file.
practice.hint: create, then the two words for what it does with time.
practice.why: createTimeSkipping starts a test server that moves its clock to the next timer whenever every workflow is only waiting.

practice.q: You want to test that a decision on the second day comes after exactly one reminder. What goes between start and signal?

options.why: It moves the test clock past the first timer, so the reminder is sent, and then the test approves on day two.
That waits 25 real hours in Node. The test server's clock is the one that must move.

options.text: Nothing; time skipping will stop at the reminder by itself
options.why: Without a pause the server would skip all the way to parking before your signal arrives.

practice.q: Finish the replay test's key line, which replays one saved history with the current code.
practice.why: runReplayHistory replays the history with the workflow code at workflowsPath and throws DeterminismViolationError on a mismatch.

practice.q: Put the steps of adding a replay test for a new path in order.
items: Run the new path once on a dev server, for example a plan that is changed and then approved
Save its history with temporal workflow show --output json into test/histories
Run the replay test and see it pass with the current code
Make your next workflow change and run the replay test again
If it fails, wrap the change in patched and run it again before you merge
practice.why: Saved histories stand for the open runs in production. The test makes every change prove that those runs will still replay.

practice.q: A test never ends and the log is full of "Activity function checkReadiness is not registered on this Worker". Why does it hang instead of failing?

options.text: The activity fails, its retry policy retries it forever, and the time-skipping server makes the retries very fast
options.why: A missing activity is an ordinary failure, so Temporal keeps retrying. Add a fake for checkReadiness.

options.text: The test server is waiting for a timer that never fires
options.why: The log shows activity attempts, not a timer. Something keeps failing and being retried.
That would show a Nondeterminism error. This is a missing function on the worker.
